candidates.name: Directed evolution with yeast surface display and alternating-pH selection
candidates.scope: Use a displayed Fcab library with positive selection for Her2 binding at pH 7.4 and negative selection/non-binding at pH 6.0, followed by clone-level pH-dependent binding characterization.

comparison.expected_value: Directly explores sequence space and can discover pH-sensitive variants without assuming histidine substitutions are required.
comparison.resources: Yeast display library, flow cytometric sorting, recombinant Her2, soluble-expression workflow and downstream binding/stability assays.
comparison.validation: Compare binding at pH 6.0 versus 7.4, then verify soluble-protein/cell binding and stability with independent repeats.
comparison.limitations: Empirical and resource-intensive; findings may depend strongly on library design, target, antibody format and selection thresholds.
comparison.novelty: Useful discovery-oriented comparator because it can reveal non-obvious pH-switching sequence solutions.

candidates.name: Structure-based dual-pH histidine-scanning computational design
candidates.scope: Use a structure-based antibody design platform with dual-pH histidine-scanning mutagenesis to propose variants, then test Fab and full-size antibody binding across acidic and physiological pH.

comparison.expected_value: Provides a targeted, mechanism-guided design route that can reduce the experimental search space and optimize acidic-pH selectivity.
comparison.resources: Antibody-antigen structural model, computational design platform, recombinant expression, binding assays, cell-based validation and functional spheroid assays.
comparison.validation: Measure recombinant and cell-surface binding across pH, compare parental controls, inspect Her2-density effects and confirm functional activity under acidic versus physiological conditions.
comparison.limitations: Depends on structural information and histidine-centered design assumptions; assay stoichiometry and avidity can affect apparent affinity estimates.
comparison.novelty: Useful design-oriented comparator because it prospectively links structural modeling to pH-selective antibody engineering.
